solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fall chasing runners in exploratory part of course

indicators.note: one thing chasing another runs behind it, so this piece comes second in the answer

parts.note: the field is all the runners in a race
to trip is to stumble and fall

explanation.surface: A runner takes a tumble while chasing the others during an exploratory stretch of a cross-country course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing runners' puts the word for Fall after the word for runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A field trip is an outing during a course of study where students explore a site first-hand.

clue.text: Flattens northern hills

definitions.meaning: second meaning: upland moors of northern England

explanation.surface: Something levels the hills in the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell is to knock flat, and fells is also the word for high hills in the Lake District and Pennines.

clue.text: This person's wearing red, exotically fur-trimmed

indicators.note: a word that is wearing another has it on, so it wraps around the other word
something done exotically is done in a strange foreign fashion, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: belonging to me, the setter
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes their own exotic red outfit with fur trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for 'This person's' sits inside a jumbled version of the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat used on robes, so a garment edged with it is ermined.

clue.text: One's wanted to stay, heading right down in fact

indicators.note: one word placed in another is enclosed by it
the head letter, an R for right, is sent down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a datum is a single given fact
to reside is to stay or live somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone eager to remain, with their mind set on going downwards, as a matter of fact.
explanation.walkthrough: The R that heads the word for 'to stay' moves to its foot, and in a down clue 'down' fits that move to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A desideratum is Latin for a thing desired, something felt to be needed or wanted.

clue.text: My family's queer-headed, it's whispered

indicators.note: a word that is headed by another has that other word placed at its front

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
belonging to my family is ours

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that someone's family is headed by an odd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer-headed' means the word for queer goes at the head of the word for 'My family's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is unverified gossip passed on quietly from person to person, hence something whispered.

clue.text: Sneakers put pressure on boat crew crossing line

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: a crew crossing something straddles it, so the crew's word goes either side of it

parts.note: the people who row a boat
L is a standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Trainers apply pressure on a rowing crew as it crosses the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneakers' looks like shoes, but means people who sneak about.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowlers are people who creep around stealthily, often with bad intent, so they are sneakers.

clue.text: Narrow beam in mine entrance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin ray, as of light
second meaning: the vertical passage leading down into a mine

explanation.surface: A thin ray of light shines into the opening of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of sunlight is a narrow ray, and a mine shaft is the vertical way into the workings.

clue.text: Regularly shifty, lie

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A shifty person tells a lie as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' is a verb here, not a fib: to rest in a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that sit somewhere rest there, as a town lies or sits in a valley.

clue.text: Revolving doors operate thus if all else fails

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a revolving door turns when given a shove
second meaning: the idiom for doing something only with great effort, as a last resort

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful literal reading of the idiom; the second is its everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if pressed or with difficulty, a fallback when nothing easier works; literally, a door moves when given a shove.

clue.text: Switch round, and profit by performances

parts.note: the take is the money made, the profit
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: Change direction and make money from your shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to alternate, switching places in rotation with someone else.

clue.text: Large expressions of doubts about terms of previous one-off payment

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: the hesitations go about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: two hesitant noises, one on each side

indicators.note: the terms of a word are its ends, its first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Doubts are expressed about the conditions of an earlier single large payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'expressions' signals two UMs, which then wrap the ends of 'previous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made all at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Available support for remote inland area

parts.note: a new book or film that is out is available
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Help is on offer for a far-off region of the interior.
explanation.definitionFit: The outback is the sparsely populated, remote interior of Australia.

clue.text: Foreign currency Spanish gents used (not ores)

indicators.note: not means the following letters are excluded from the word

parts.note: señores is Spanish for gentlemen
the letters to drop, taken as written

explanation.surface: Spanish gentlemen paid in a foreign currency rather than in raw minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The sen is a small coin, a hundredth of the Japanese yen and of other Asian currencies.

clue.text: Court problem — ball out, feud developing

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: On a tennis court, a ball called out starts a row between players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A double fault in tennis is two failed serves in a row, losing the server the point.

clue.text: Accomplished cricket side well and truly defeated

parts.note: a finished performer is accomplished, polished
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A skilful cricket team was thoroughly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg (or on) side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be finished off is to be killed or completely beaten, given the final blow.

clue.text: Iron lady's soft hat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a woman's name

explanation.surface: The Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher, wears a soft hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron lady' evokes Thatcher, but the two words are split; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a felt hat with a soft brim and a creased crown.

clue.text: Grief, pint being spilt in joint

definitions.note: loosely, the end segment of a finger

indicators.note: spilt drink splashes everywhere, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at a pint knocked over in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a pub or a cut of meat; here it is a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The fingertip is the last segment of the finger, a joint in the sense of a jointed section.

clue.text: Historic food platter for one digging in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a medieval wooden plate or slab of bread for serving food
second meaning: someone who digs trenches

explanation.surface: An old serving dish is put out for someone tucking into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digging in' suggests eating heartily, but means digging ditches.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher was a medieval plate, and literally one who trenches is a ditch-digger.

clue.text: Flash old king's formal supporter

parts.note: in a flash means in a second, a moment
ER is Edward Rex, as on old royal insignia

explanation.surface: A showy former monarch is someone's official backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder formally supports a motion proposed at a meeting so it can be debated.

clue.text: Refinement expected of men at smart weddings?

definitions.note: a singular abstract noun defining a plural, fair because refinement as a quality is made up of many such fine points

parts.words: Refinement expected of men at smart weddings?
parts.note: surface reading: the polished manners expected of male wedding guests

parts.words: expected of men at smart weddings
parts.note: setter's reading: what men wear round their necks at a smart wedding, split into two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NICE TIES, the smart neckwear men wear to weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine points of etiquette and subtle distinctions, the details of refinement.

clue.text: Make allowances, keeping it up with increasing rancour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: to cater for something is to allow for it
taken as written, then turned around

explanation.surface: Making allowances while keeping going even as resentment grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattier means more spiteful and malicious, showing greater rancour than before.

clue.text: Huge flower one revered beside the Nile

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
the iris is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A giant bloom is worshipped on the banks of the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' could be a river, which the Nile reinforces, but here it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god of the dead, worshipped along the Nile.

clue.text: Transport engineers first to prepare for new job?

indicators.note: first tells you the engineers' piece goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Railway engineers are the first to get ready for a fresh job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers first' tells you their letters go before those for transport.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn new skills, preparing oneself for a different kind of work.

clue.text: Spooner's to chuck out dismal sailor

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: to chuck out is to bin and dismal is sad; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: Someone wants to throw out a gloomy seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BIN SAD to get SIN BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the legendary sailor of the Arabian Nights tales and his seven voyages.

clue.text: Sexier rogue grabbing time to make up

indicators.note: a rogue goes off course and misbehaves, so these letters run out of order
grabbing something means seizing it and holding it inside

parts.note: the letters rearranged
tempo is the timing or speed of music

explanation.surface: A sexy rascal takes time to apply cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' tempts as cosmetics, but means invent on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To extemporise is to improvise, making something up as you go without preparation.

clue.text: Cat bell

explanation.walkthrough: Great Tom is the famous bell in Tom Tower at Christ Church, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, and several big church bells are named Tom.

clue.text: Mum and daughter subdued

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means silent
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother and her daughter are both quiet and restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted colours or reactions are subdued, toned down or softened.

clue.text: Success in returning what's owed for furniture

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it
returning means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a debt is money owed, then turned around
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A winner receives back money owed to them to buy furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin bed is one of a matching pair of single beds, an item of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Extra Times edition's leader

parts.note: by is the word for times in multiplication, as in three by four

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A special issue of The Times newspaper carries a lead article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper setting this puzzle, but means multiplied by. In cricket, an extra is a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, one of the cricket extras.

clue.text: Floating duck acquired by shop for social worker

indicators.note: something acquired by another is taken into its possession, so it sits inside

parts.note: to shop is to buy
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A floating duck is bought by a pet shop on behalf of a care worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a care professional but an ant, which lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant means able to float, staying up on the surface of water.

clue.text: Authentic English pulp

parts.note: pure means genuine, unadulterated
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Genuine English mush, perhaps from a traditional kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is food crushed or blended into a smooth pulp.

clue.text: Polished, cut by editor then specified another way

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other wedged into the gap

parts.note: refined means polished, cultivated
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A text is polished and trimmed by its editor, then reworded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests editing out, but here the editor is inserted after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to state its meaning or terms anew, differently from before.
